_rule: Every target is a hub, never a specific story. A story-level target requires PROVABLE equivalence — same protagonist AND same theme — and none of the four dead stories has a live successor that clears that bar. See _why_hubs_not_stories.
_why_hubs_not_stories: Checked by diffing the old hook against every live hook (git show bdc0c2f4:lib/stories.ts). All four dead stories share only a MOTIF with a live story, never the story itself: the-tangled-kite (Finn, friendship/asking for help) shares 'a kite stuck in a tree' with bunnys-big-feelings (Bunny, emotional regulation); milos-little-boat (Milo, patience/building) shares only the word 'boat' with the-brave-little-boat (an anthropomorphic red boat, courage in a storm). Redirecting a parent who searched a specific title to a different book is a wrong answer; the catalog is an honest one.

redirects.reason: Old hook: "Fly, kite, fly! Then the string slips — and Finn's bright kite is stuck high in a tree. One friend isn't enough." Protagonist Finn, theme is friendship and asking for help. NOT bunnys-big-feelings, which stars Bunny and is about big feelings — they share a kite motif, not a story.

Old hook: "All summer he built it. Tonight, under the moon, Milo's leaf-and-twig boat finally sails." Protagonist Milo (a boy), theme is patience and building something. NOT the-brave-little-boat, whose protagonist is an anthropomorphic red boat facing a storm — they share the word 'boat' and nothing else.
Old hook: "Crickets, bees, and rustling leaves — the bedtime concert every night. One frog hiding behind a leaf, sure her voice sounds funny." Theme is stage fright. No live story comes near it.
No live successor. Nothing in the current catalog shares its setting or theme.
